rows: Tornado caused three injuries due to a large oak tree falling through a home at Fair Oaks Ranch on the Old Spanish Road. Significant damage to a chicken farm located east of Normangee which killed 15,000 chickens. Numerous trees down, several damaged roofs, and downed power lines…
Tree down on the Old Spanish Road at FM 1452 in the northwest corner of the county.
A thunderstorm wind gust estimated at 52 knots downed a tree.
There were trees downed along Highway 39 in North Zulch.
A tree fell on a mobile home that caused roof damage at the 300 block of Harrell Street. There were also a few trees reported down throughout the town of Madisonville.
Thunderstorm winds downed a power pole along Highway 21.
Nickel-sized hail was reported on FM 1428.
A brief touchdown was observed near North Zulch in rural Madison County. This was the second reported tornado with this particular thunderstorm.
Storm chasers from Texas A&M University observed a brief touchdown east of their location on FM 39 south of Highway 21. This was the third and final reported tornado with this thunderstorm.
Power lines were felled by high winds.
Downed trees were reported along FM 1428.
Severe thunderstorm damaged large trees with some trees up to one foot in diameter snapped.

Severe thunderstorm winds tore the roofs off of several businesses and numerous other structures and residences suffered lesser damage. Emergency management officials reported 22 businesses and 22 homes sustained damage.
Severe thunderstorm winds overturned several vehicles on Interstate 45 near Madisonville and toppled or snapped 50 to 75 trees on a farm along Hwy 75 southeast of Madisonville.
Severe thunderstorm produced quarter sized hailstones that covered the ground.
Winds estimated at 80 MPH with severe thunderstorm in Madisonville.
A severe thunderstorm produced nickel size hail.
Downed trees from severe thunderstorm winds ended up blocking the road.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees on Highway 21 between Midway and the Trinity River.
A severe thunderstorm produced half dollar size hail approximately 2 miles south of Highway 21.
Strong downburst winds destroyed at least two barns and blew metal sheeting 200 to 300 yards toward the northeast. A large tank was also knocked over.

Severe thunderstorm winds damaged a barn and destroyed a tin shed near the intersection of FM 1452 and FM 2289 west of Madisonville.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew over an 18 wheeler truck on Interstate 45 around the 145 mile marker.
There were multiple reports of trees down. Roofs were lost on some metal and wood buildings off of Highway 21.
There were reports of numerous trees downed around the county.
There was golf ball size hail near the the intersection of Old San Antonio Road and Highway 75.
There was dime to quarter size hail observed.
Severe thunderstorm winds downed trees in the southern portions of the county.
Golfball sized hail was observed approximately 12 miles west of Madisonville.
Quarter sized hail was observed just off to the east northeast of Madisonville.
A severe thunderstorm caused isolated roof and tree damage in and around the OSR area to the northwest through north of the North Zulch area.
Nickel sized hail was reported to the east of Madisonville.
Thunderstorm winds downed some trees on Mary Street and Shady Creek Lane.
EF-0 tornado briefly touched down in the North Zulch area and damaged some trees from Bundic Road to Diserens Road.
Golf ball sized hail was reported between the Madisonville and Midway areas.
Nickel sized hail was reported near the intersection of Interstate 45 and Highway 21.
Downed and uprooted trees stretched from the Madisonville Junior High School area southeastward for a couple miles in and around Pee Dee Lane.
Quarter sized hail was reported near Midway.
Multiple reports of trees down across parts of Madison County including Highway 21 West near Midway.
Golf ball sized hail was reported.
Baseball sized hail was reported on US 190 west of Madisonville.
Part of a building was blocking Highway 39 between OSR and Batson Loop.
There were multiple reports of quarter size hail.
Trees were downed at the Madisonville library.

There was ping pong ball sized hail near Madisonville.
Golf ball to ping pong ball sized hail occurred near Madisonville.
A tree was downed across the road at the intersection of FM 39 and FM 1452.
Half dollar sized hail was observed.
Trees downed throughout the Madisonville area.
Glass windows were broken at a local business.
Wind gust was measured at K5PNV.

NWS Storm survey found EF1 tornado damage along a path across portions of northern Grimes and southern Madison counties, generally parallel and to the west of SH 90 between Bedias and Madisonville. Damage included trees downed and uprooted, and there was also some roof damage to …
Golf ball sized hail was observed in the Cottonwood area.
Wind gust occurred at the SH 75 S Tempest Weather system site.
Wind gust occurred at the SH 75 S Tempest weather system site.
Numerous trees and fences were downed in the Normangee area.
Trees were downed near North Zulch.
A large tree was downed near the intersection of FM 1428 and Highway 21.
Hail was reported via MPING near Connor.

Broadcast media reported wind damage in Madisonville, including Tractor Supply Company and areas along FM 1452 east. A barn was destroyed and several buildings were damaged. Peak wind speeds were estimated at 94 mph based on a small barn with a degree of damage of 8.
